results.reason: Issue 3 identifies that SA §13.2 lets Norvane assign to any third party without notice while Calder Ridge needs consent. It explains the risk of drawings and supply passing to a competitor or weak assignee, and proposes mutual consent plus a competitor carve-out.

Identifies the §13.3 consent and termination right on a change of control and explains the leverage it gives Norvane over a sale or merger. It recommends deleting the clause or limiting it to competitor acquirers. It does treat the sale as hypothetical rather than pending, but the core analysis and fix are present.
Identifies the OF §2.2 auto-renewal for 3-year terms on 30 days' notice and explains the lock-in risk. It proposes 1-year renewals, 90-day notice and a reminder obligation.
Notes that §9.3 exempts only Calder Ridge's indemnity from the cap, while Norvane's indemnity is capped. It recommends a mutual carve-out and narrowing §10.1.
Correctly states the cap as fees paid in the prior 12 months, Delaware law under §12.1, and a 3-year Initial Term from March 1, 2026.
Correctly states the SA > OF > Schedule precedence and applies it to the renewal conflict (SA §2.1 vs. OF §2.2) and the invoice-timing conflict.
The priority table ranks the indemnity as Critical and change of control as High, ahead of the lesser issues.
Each issue is structured with Where / Why it matters / Fix and proposed language. A separate Business Questions section appears at the end.

Flags the Specifications Schedule as a Critical issue (product mismatch). It also raises Schedule-based concerns about the AQL sampling plan, head standards, inspection rejection and the 'Acknowledged' signature block, treating the distractor document as containing significant issues.
